binders: An arbitrary type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with an IsProbabilityMeasure instance.
A sequence X : Nat → Ω → Real of real-valued random variables.
A source-facing proof hσ that 0 < σ.
A source-facing family hX proving MemLp (X i) 2 μ for every natural i.
A source-facing proof hIndep that the family X is mutually independent under μ.
A source-facing family hIdent proving X i and X 0 are identically distributed under μ for every natural i.
A source-facing equality hMean stating integral of X 0 with respect to μ equals m.
A source-facing equality hVariance stating variance of X 0 under μ equals σ².
hypotheses: Every X_i is square-integrable with respect to μ.
The indexed family X is mutually independent.
Every X_i has the same distribution as X_0.
conclusions: LocalDef001 μ X m σ hσ hX hIndep hIdent hMean hVariance holds if and only if, for every real threshold t, the probability that the (N + 1)-term normalized centered sum is at most t converges as N tends to infinity to the standard-normal probability of (-∞, t].
Formally, for every t : Real, Tendsto (fun N => Law(S_{N+1})(Set.Iic t)) atTop (nhds (StandardNormal(Set.Iic t))).
The outer result is an iff, and LocalDef001 unfolds to this same every-threshold convergence condition.
mathematical_definitions: For n : Nat and ω : Ω, S_n(ω) = (1 / (σ sqrt(n))) * sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (X_i(ω) - m).
The sequence used in the convergence criterion is S_{N+1}, so every denominator is σ sqrt(N + 1) and every numerator contains the first N + 1 centered variables.
Law(S_n) is the pushforward of μ by S_n, bundled as a probability measure using almost-everywhere measurability.
The limiting law is gaussianReal 0 1, bundled as a probability measure; this is the standard-normal probability law.
Set.Iic t is the lower closed interval (-∞, t], so evaluating a law on Set.Iic t gives its CDF value at t.
Convergence in distribution here is defined by convergence of these CDF values for every real threshold t along Filter.atTop.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any probability space and any real-valued sequence X with the supplied positivity, square-integrability, independence, identical-distribution, mean, and variance data, the named convergence-in-distribution predicate is equivalent to the following explicit condition: at every real threshold t, the probability that the normalized sum of the first N + 1 centered variables, divided by σ times the square root of N + 1, is at most t tends as N goes to infinity to the corresponding standard-normal probability. This equivalence is definitional because the named predicate unfolds to that condition.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The declaration is a definitional iff: the left-hand predicate unfolds to essentially the right-hand statement, so it does not itself prove a central limit theorem from the probabilistic assumptions.
The definition body computationally ignores hσ, hIndep, hIdent, hMean, and hVariance; these remain source-facing context binders but do not drive the displayed CDF convergence condition.
The MemLp hypotheses are used to obtain almost-everywhere measurability and hence define pushforward probability laws, but square-integrability is not used to establish convergence.

The criterion quantifies over every real threshold, rather than merely continuity points of a general limiting CDF. For the standard normal this is mathematically compatible because its CDF is continuous, but that continuity is not stated in the target.
Using N + 1 avoids the n = 0 normalization, where sqrt(0) and reciprocal conventions would otherwise make the formula degenerate.
Although hσ guarantees a positive normalizing scale, the explicit RHS does not use that proof to simplify or justify division; Real inversion is total in Lean.
No conclusion asserts that the convergence condition actually holds; the proposition only characterizes the named predicate by its unfolded formula.
ambiguities: The Gaussian constructor's second parameter is an NNReal variance parameter according to the supplied dependency type; at value 1 it unambiguously yields the standard normal law.
The notation for probability-measure evaluation returns NNReal rather than Real, so Tendsto occurs in the topology of NNReal; semantically these are ordinary probability values.
The hidden proof argument passed when constructing each normalized-sum law is proof-irrelevant mathematically and supplies only almost-everywhere measurability.
